newsitem.title: UK: LME base metals steady to firmer in pre-market.
newsitem.headline: LME base metals steady to firmer in pre-market.

text.p: London Metal Exchange (LME) base metal prices were steady to firmer on Tuesday morning after U.K. markets reopened after a long holiday weekend.
Early inter-office trade was generally quiet except for a burst of short-covering in zinc, traders said.
"The markets have done reasonably well, but they're still in range," a trader noted. "People are unsure of what's going to happen next."
Copper prices were meandering in the high end of a $2,320-$2,380 range, traders said.
Three months copper ticked higher and was last at $2,374, per tonne compared to Friday's kerb close of $2,360. Cash to threes backwardation was also $7 wider at $67/$77.
An LME stock increase of 1,000 tonnes was not enough to turn prices lower, and an ongoing strike at the Quebrada Blanca pit in Chile was supportive, traders said.
But some traders suspected the upside was limited unless fund buying injected interest into a market approaching the summer lull.
"It took a backwardation of $200 to get copper where it is and it's going to take the re-emergence of the funds to get it to $2,400," a trader said.
Aluminum was also higher at $1,635, compared to $1,624 on Friday. An LME stock fall of 2,625 tonnes was underpinning the market. Last week inventories fell nearly 12,000 tonnes.
Analysts said aluminium was trading in a $1,620-$1,650 band and only a breach of either end would signal a break of out range.
Zinc traded up to $1,274, up $12 from Friday's kerb close, on shortcovering from off-market players.
Resistance is pegged at $1,280 and then $1,290.
The other metals showed little spark in the pre-market.
Tin was indicated virtually unchanged at $5,730/50, as was lead at $622/25.
Nickel was similarly steady at $7,430/50, as was alloy at $1,500/$1,510.
